obligation: FSIS notification of adulterated or misbranded product in commerce
trigger: Establishment learns or determines that adulterated or misbranded meat product received by or originating from it has entered commerce (for example, product shipped while cook, chill, or cold storage CCPs were unmonitored or controls were tampered with, and evaluation finds it adulterated)
deadline: Within 24 hours of learning or determining; include type, amount, origin, and destination of the product

trigger: Responsible party (the registrant of a food facility) determines an article of food is a reportable food: reasonable probability that its use or exposure will cause serious adverse health consequences or death. Applies to the FDA-regulated seafood products
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 24 hours after the determination. No report is required if the adulteration originated with the company, was detected before any transfer to another person, and was corrected or the food destroyed (350f(d)(2))
notify: FDA through the Reportable Food Registry electronic portal; also investigate the cause

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee data held by the company or its payroll vendor; online store customer accounts)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if personal information is accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
A vendor maintaining personal information for the company (payroll vendor, e-commerce vendor) discovers a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company within 10 days of determination

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state); online store customers outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to FBI and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0 to Day 2 in the runbook)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and may bring OT response help

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-26; as proposed the company is below the size criterion (250 employees vs. 1,000-employee SBA standard) and Food and Agriculture has no sector criterion. Recheck when final

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident at an MTSA-regulated facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); 'without delay' to the National Response Center for entities not reporting under 6.16-1
notify: FBI, CISA (for any cyber incident), and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - the plant is not an MTSA-regulated facility

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - Cris Santos Company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Ammonia release reporting (only if the incident causes a release)
citation: Not verified in this sample (federal and state release-reporting rules for anhydrous ammonia)
trigger: Loss of refrigeration control leads to an ammonia release
deadline: Not stated here; follow the PSM and RMP emergency response plan
notify: Per the site emergency response plan
applies_at_this_tier: Conditional - refrigeration is in scope of the incident

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

trigger: Incident affecting product safety, delivery, or customer data
deadline: Per each agreement (commonly prompt notice of any recall or food safety event)
